gaps.sentence: We haven't got ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough chairs' means a sufficient number; 'too' before the noun would give the wrong meaning and position.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: ___ single room in the hotel was fully booked.
gaps.explanation: 'Every single room' is the emphatic collocation meaning 'without exception'.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ enthusiasm for the proposal, so it was quietly shelved.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' (without 'a') means not enough — which explains shelving the proposal.
'Luggage' is an uncountable noun, so 'how much' is used.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the students has been given a personal timetable.
gaps.hint: this is the only option that can be followed by 'of' and take a singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each of the students has ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' here and 'all/both' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ of the villagers had ever seen a passport.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly any of' = almost none of; 'hardly none' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: The village is remote and has ___ facilities — not even a post office.
gaps.hint: negative meaning with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Few facilities' means almost none, which matches 'not even a post office'; 'facilities' is countable.
